summary: 1. Open instantly with second-person sensory immersion ('सोचो, तुम्हारे...' or 'तुम...') rather than passive introductory statements. 2. Lead the very first sentence with a visceral paradox or mind-bending physical comparison (e.g., '3 cars stacked on teeth', 'crumpling protects you') within 5 words. 3. Eliminate technical jargon and academic framing like 'hydroplaning' or 'वैज्ञानिकों को ऐसी सूक्ष्म आकृतियां मिली' from titles and opening lines. 4. Keep titles written in conversational Devanagari mixed with common English nouns plus a single contextual emoji (e.g., 🦖 or 🚗), avoiding full English or textbook Hindi phrasing. 5. Cap target duration near 25–35 seconds; all 40s+ videos suffered sub-38% stayed rates due to slow setups.
winning_hooks: Direct Physical Paradox: 'जो car crash में पिचक जाती है, वो तुम्हें ज़्यादा बचाती है।' (66.8% stayed - presents a counter-intuitive survival truth immediately)
Extreme Physical Scale Hook: 'सोचो, तुम्हारे दांतों पर 3 छोटी cars एक के ऊपर एक रख दी जाएं...' (67.7% stayed - anchors abstract force to a bizarre, tangible image)
Identity Shift / Roleplay Hook: 'सोचो, तुम एक baby tyrannosaur हो, बस एक छोटे कुत्ते जितने।' (49.1% stayed - forces viewer self-insertion immediately)
avoid: Full-English textbook titles (e.g., 'Common Household Items That Contain Radioactive Materials' - 6.7% stayed).
Third-person scientific reporting openings ('डायनासोर के जीवाश्मों में वैज्ञानिकों को ऐसी सूक्ष्म आकृतियां...' - 37.0% stayed).
Academic or mechanical jargon in the hook before explaining stakes ('hydroplaning' - 30.6% stayed).
Mundane domestic routine questions lacking high danger or stakes ('राजमा रात भर फ्रिज में रखने के बाद...' - 25.0% stayed).
next_experiment: A/B test a single topic with: (A) Visceral 'सोचो, तुम...' roleplay hook under 30 seconds vs (B) Direct paradox claim hook ('जो चीज तुम्हें मार सकती है...') under 30 seconds, measuring whether roleplay beats paradox on stayed_pct beyond 65%.
